evidence.summary: process_run is a process_grant effect for explicit argv, bounded environment, stdin, output limits, deadline, and exit status.
Verifier execution still crosses the Python Runner so it can realize systemd/cgroup policy and owned-tree cleanup.
The exact missing compatible contract is a resource envelope and interruptible execution handle, not process spawning itself.

metadata.pressure_boundary: process capability exists but Forge cannot preserve the required generic resource and cancellation contract through process_run

reproduction.instructions: Inspect current Forge Runner and mncs.std.process.v1; the old no-process-spawning statement is false, but consumer migration remains blocked by the separately recorded resource/cancellation contract pressure.

summary: Profile 0.18 process_run remains a real process_grant capability with bounded typed request/result. Forge has not moved verifier process execution onto it because it cannot express aggregate cgroup limits or a cancellable in-flight handle; Python remains the Linux realization adapter.

workaround.description: Forge Runner continues as the bounded host process realization adapter; native resource policy is authoritative.
